page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.c6.8xlarge is a compute-optimized instance featuring 32 dedicated vCPUs and 64 GB of system memory. Powered by an Intel Xeon 8269CY processor operating at a base frequency of 2.5 GHz, the server consists of 16 physical cores with 2.0 threads per core. Memory capacity is allocated at a 1:2 RAM-to-vCPU ratio, providing 2.0 GB per vCPU. The hardware supports instruction set extensions including AVX-512 with VNNI, AES cryptography, and FMA. This instance does not include local NVMe storage or discrete GPUs, relying on network-attached storage and providing a 10 Gbps baseline network bandwidth under a KVM hypervisor.

Performance data indicates a distinct split between single-core and multi-core efficiency. Single-threaded metrics fall in the lower percentile, demonstrated by a stress-ng single-core result of 1312.39 and single-threaded gzip compression of 22.88 GB/sec. Conversely, multi-threaded operations scale effectively across all virtual cores, achieving average benchmark results such as a stress-ng multi-core score of 27992.16 and a Geekbench multi-core score of 10181.0. Memory bandwidth reaches 109.69 GB/sec for uncached large-block reads and 47.96 GB/sec for uncached writes. Specialized operational metrics include 26.78 million operations per second on Redis SET benchmarks and 20.38 GB/sec static web serving throughput.

From an engineering and qualitative cost perspective, the instance provides high parallel resource density without requiring investments in specialized GPU hardware or local NVMe storage. Workloads constrained by single-threaded clock rates may experience latency bottlenecks. However, tasks capable of leveraging multi-core parallelization benefit from predictable dedicated CPU allocations. Recommended workload fits include software compilation pipelines, parallel data processing, high-concurrency caching layers such as Redis, static web serving, and general compute-bound microservices.
